method: Primary-source web research, council democracy portals (moderngov / opencouncil.network for LCC, Worcestershire, Doncaster, Warwickshire) + local-press coverage (Blog Preston, KentOnline, Lichfield Live, Northamptonshire Telegraph, Express & Star, LGC, ITV regional, GBNews, BBC, Yorkshire Post, Left Foot Forward, Byline Times, Palatinate, ShepwayVox, Banbury FM) + national press / think-tank summaries (LSE Grantham Research Institute, UKFactCheck) + Reform-aligned outlets (Conservative Home, GB News).
scope: Motions tabled at Full Council / AGM meetings of Reform-controlled English councils. Covers the May-2025 cohort (May 2025 to 16 Jun 2026, incl. a gap-fill of Lancashire CC Oct+Nov 2025 and Apr-Jun 2026 motions across the cohort) AND the May-2026 cohort (won 7 May 2026, AGMs late May 2026) up to 16 Jun 2026. Executive/leader decisions (flag policies, Pride defunding, Lord's-Prayer-by-constitution-report) are listed separately in 'executive_and_non_motion_items', NOT counted as motions. Many May-2026 cohort motions are tabled but not yet voted (status=pending_vote) or only signalled (status=signalled_future). NOTE: Worcestershire CC LOST Reform control on 14 May 2026 (no-confidence in Leader Jo Monk; Green-led from that date). REFRESH 6 Jul 2026: outcomes verified for the 15 pending motions where minutes/webcasts/press now exist (Sunderland City of Sanctuary still unconfirmed - no minutes); window 16 Jun - 6 Jul 2026 swept across the cohort (only Wakefield 17 Jun, Sunderland 24 Jun, Walsall 22 Jun and Leicestershire 1 Jul met; Leicestershire motions added); July agendas already published were captured as pending_vote (Newcastle-under-Lyme 8 Jul x4, Nottinghamshire 9 Jul x2). Re-sweep after the mid-late July meeting cycle: NuL 8 Jul, Notts 9 Jul, Durham 15 Jul, Kent + Suffolk + Worcestershire + Gateshead + Barnsley + Doncaster 16 Jul, Warwickshire 21 Jul, St Helens + Calderdale 22 Jul, Sandwell 28 Jul, South Tyneside 30 Jul.

motions.motion_title: Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG)
motions.motion_text_summary: Commit the council to work with the Police and Crime Commissioner and Government on tackling VAWG, continue funding for specialist services, and appoint a Lead Member or Member Champion for VAWG. Reform amendment (Cllr Maria Jones) added language on coercive control, psychological, mental, emotional, financial, physical, sexual, cultural and post-separation abuse, and required the champion to have lived or work experience; accepted by mover.

motions.motion_title: Flying Flags
motions.mover: Cllr Joshua Roberts (Cabinet Member for Rural Affairs, Environment and Communities)
motions.motion_text_summary: Prioritise the flying of the Union Flag, the Flag of England, the Lancashire Flag, royal flags, military flags and ensigns at County Hall and other council property; Cabinet to review the flag policy to ensure individual political causes do not take precedence over shared identity. Independent amendment (Cllr Azhar Ali) to route review through Community, Cultural and Corporate Services Scrutiny Committee, rejected by mover, defeated.

motions.motion_title: First Past the Post Voting System
motions.motion_text_summary: Sought to replace First Past the Post for local and general elections. Lib Dem amendment (Cllr David Whipp) to add AV for mayoral and STV for multi-member wards, rejected by mover. Original motion defeated.

motions.motion_title: Free Speech
motions.motion_text_summary: Resolved the council foster a culture of free speech across Lancashire. Independent amendment (Cllr Azhar Ali) added compliance with UK law and the Nolan Principles, and the proviso that speech must not incite hatred and division, accepted by mover.

motions.motion_title: Condemnation of any move to scrap Northern Powerhouse Rail
motions.motion_text_summary: Condemnation of any attempts to scrap or de-fund Northern Powerhouse Rail; call on Government to ringfence funding. Passed at the budget-setting meeting alongside approval of the 2026/27 council-tax precept.

motions.motion_title: Rescind Climate Emergency Declaration
motions.motion_text_summary: Rescind the council's Climate Emergency declaration. Motion narrative noted 'the unproven view of anthropogenic (human-induced) climate change' and stated the council had had 'no discernible affect on the world's climate.' Effect: removes obligation to consider net-zero and cancels existing net-zero policies. Second UK upper-tier authority to rescind, after Durham.

motions.motion_title: Approval of the Strategic Statement 'Reforming Kent 2025-2028'
motions.motion_text_summary: Approve the Reform UK group's Strategic Statement 'Reforming Kent 2025-2028' as the council's overarching strategy. Structured around debt reduction, LGR business case and a 'Kent-first' residents-first approach.

motions.motion_title: Centre VAWG in planning + White Ribbon accreditation
motions.motion_text_summary: Sought to place VAWG at the centre of KCC thinking (planning, etc.) and to commit to continued White Ribbon accreditation. Voted down by the Reform majority.

motions.motion_title: Declare an 'Illegal Migration Emergency in Kent'
motions.motion_text_summary: Sought formal declaration of an 'Illegal Migration Emergency in Kent' on the basis of small-boat pressure. Five-page supporting report claimed arrivals are 'likely to contain a number of potential terrorist cells, supporting IS and al-Qaeda'. Demanded Labour Government halt small-boat arrivals and fund full local cost. Supporting evidence criticised as factually unsupported; motion did not pass.

motions.meeting_type: Member Committee, referred to Full Council
motions.motion_title: Recite Lord's Prayer + sing national anthem at the start of Full Council meetings
motions.vote_result: Referred to Full Council (passed at committee stage; amendment allowing prayer in livestream also passed)
motions.motion_text_summary: Amend the order of business so each Full Council meeting opens with the Lord's Prayer and the national anthem. Monitoring Officer warned the prayer could not lawfully be included in the official livestream; amendment passed to allow it. NSS and Green / Lib Dem groups urging rejection.

motions.motion_title: Remove Pride flag and Ukrainian flag from County Hall and chamber
motions.motion_text_summary: Reform administration announced council would no longer fly the Pride flag during Pride Month, and removed the Ukrainian flag from the council chamber; Leader Linden Kemkaran described the Ukrainian flag in the chamber as 'a distraction'.

motions.motion_title: Rescind Climate Emergency Declaration + declare County Durham Care Emergency
motions.mover: Cllr Darren Grimes (Reform UK, Deputy Leader)
motions.motion_text_summary: Rescind Durham County Council's 2019 climate emergency declaration; declare a 'County Durham Care Emergency' prioritising support to vulnerable children and adult social care. First UK council to formally reverse a climate emergency declaration.

motions.motion_title: Remove Pride flag from County Hall + defund Durham Pride
motions.motion_text_summary: Day-one Reform action: Pride flag removed from County Hall by Deputy Leader Cllr Darren Grimes (described as 'anti-tokenism'). Council subsequently (Aug 2025) withdrew Durham Pride funding; Deputy Leader: 'taxpayers should not fund political street theatre'.

motions.motion_title: Free Speech / Article 10 ECHR protections in the Code of Conduct
motions.motion_text_summary: Incorporate the principle that 'there is no right to not be offended by lawful speech' into the Code of Conduct; give 'particular regard' to enhanced protection for political speech under Article 10 ECHR; prevent 'vexatious' standards proceedings.

motions.motion_title: Flag policy: restrict council buildings to Union Flag only
motions.motion_text_summary: Revise the corporate flag protocol so only the Union Flag is flown, with exceptions for the Royal Standard when the King is present and for national flags of visiting heads of state. 'Council property belongs to all residents and should reflect our shared national identity, not particular causes, campaigns, or interest groups.' Mayor Ros Jones (Labour) refused to enact. At least 3 Reform councillors did not vote for (Craig Ward, Brendan Megaw + abstainer).

motions.motion_title: Motion of No Confidence in Mayor Ros Jones over Doncaster Sheffield Airport
motions.mover: Cllr Guy Aston (Reform UK group leader)
motions.motion_text_summary: Symbolic no-confidence motion: 'The Mayor's repeated pledges on Doncaster Sheffield Airport have not been delivered and have misled the public as to the timescales and certainty of reopening.' Mayor model means motion has no executive effect.

motions.motion_title: Adopt revised Green Masterplan dropping 2050 carbon-neutral target
motions.motion_text_summary: Adopt new Green Masterplan dropping the 2050 carbon-neutral aspiration as 'unachievable' and commits to cutting emissions only where central government funding covers the cost. Meeting twice disrupted by Extinction Rebellion protesters. Note: Lincolnshire never declared a climate emergency, so the policy lever is the target itself, not a declaration.

motions.meeting_type: Joint press conference (not Full Council motion)
motions.motion_title: Launch 'Lincolnshire Opposes Renewable Eyesores' (LORE) campaign vs 'net-stupid-zero'
motions.group: Reform (administration) + Greater Lincolnshire Mayor Andrea Jenkyns
motions.vote_result: Political launch / policy direction; subsequently expressed at planning level
motions.motion_text_summary: Joint press conference launched LORE, a political campaign opposing new solar farms, battery storage and pylons in Lincolnshire. Coupled with public statements that climate emergency is not real.

motions.motion_title: Freeze councillors' Basic Allowances + cut Conservative Leader Special Responsibility Allowance
motions.mover: Cllr Alan Graves (Reform UK, Council Leader)
motions.motion_text_summary: Freeze all councillors' Basic Allowances at the 2025-26 level for 2026-27, citing cost-of-living pressures and pending LGR. Controversial bolt-on: cut Conservative Opposition Leader Alex Dale's Special Responsibility Allowance by a third, from £18,840 to £12,560. Opposition called this 'gutter politics' and 'full Donald Trump'. Allowance freeze is the clean political-class-cuts play; the SRA cut is the riskier partisan add-on.

motions.motion_title: Approve 4.9% increase to council tax precept for 2026-27
motions.motion_text_summary: Approve a 4.9% council-tax precept increase, contrary to repeated Reform election-campaign signals that the party would freeze or cut council tax. Triggered Full Fact piece flagging broken pre-election promises.

motions.motion_title: Rescind Climate Change Emergency Declaration (2019)
motions.mover: Cllr Andrew Mynors (Cabinet Member for Connectivity)
motions.motion_text_summary: Rescind the 2019 Climate Change Emergency Declaration. Replace with a new environmental strategy focused on 'value for money' and immediate local impact. Motion text: 'Rather than chasing long-term targets we will focus on protecting and enhancing our environment and the impacts we can have now, particularly if they can deliver value for money for our communities, businesses and the county council.' Lone Green Cllr Jack Rose flagged Cllr Mynors' employment with BDM Geolog UK Ltd (oil/gas/geothermal); Monitoring Officer concluded interest was properly declared. New environmental strategy (Dec 2025) does not mention climate change.

motions.motion_title: Withdraw from Midlands Connect Consortium
motions.motion_text_summary: Withdraw Staffordshire County Council from the Midlands Connect transport-strategy consortium. Aligns with Reform's 'reduce subscriptions to regional partnership bodies' theme.

motions.motion_title: Spend £75,000 putting up Union flags on county lampposts
motions.motion_text_summary: Approve £75,000 capital allocation to install Union flags on lampposts across Nottinghamshire. Leader defended the spend amid criticism it was symbolic at the expense of services.

motions.meeting_type: Cabinet / public statement (no Full Council motion to rescind)
motions.motion_title: De-prioritise net zero / 2030 carbon-neutral commitment
motions.mover: Cllr Bert Bingham (Cabinet Member for Transport and Environment)
motions.motion_text_summary: Cabinet Member Bert Bingham publicly described man-made climate change as a 'hoax' and stated intention to 'end the net zero crime'. Council has NOT yet tabled a Full Council motion to rescind the 2021 declaration, LSE Grantham Institute notes risks of legal challenge + loss of climate-tied grant funding. So Notts's play is de-emphasis-by-cabinet rather than formal rescission.

motions.motion_title: Reaffirm Climate Emergency Declaration (2019)
motions.motion_text_summary: Confirm and reaffirm the climate emergency declared by Warwickshire in 2019. Green motion with a Conservative friendly amendment. Opposed by Reform group. Carried 32-22 with one Reform abstention. Warwickshire is the ONE 13-May-2025 council where the Reform group failed to defeat a pro-climate motion, because Reform governs as a minority and the Conservatives backed the Greens.

motions.motion_title: Reaffirm cycling/walking + bus + Warwickshire Rail Strategy
motions.motion_text_summary: Reaffirm support for local cycling/walking infrastructure investment, bus services improvement strategy and Warwickshire Rail Strategy. Backed despite Council Leader George Finch's public characterisation of cycleways as 'a waste of money'.

motions.motion_title: Support for Town and Parish Councils + role in preserving local identity
motions.motion_text_summary: Endorse town and parish councils' role in preserving local identity; commit to devolving powers downward where there is local community appetite.

motions.motion_title: Single Unitary Council for Warwickshire (LGR)
motions.motion_text_summary: Single unitary council covering all of Warwickshire is the optimum LGR model; full constituent membership of West Midlands Combined Authority is the optimum devolution arrangement. Lib Dem amendment citing 73% of survey respondents preferring two unitary authorities, defeated.

motions.motion_title: Healthcare Parking Permit Scheme
motions.motion_text_summary: Develop proposals for a county-wide healthcare parking permit scheme allowing verified healthcare professionals to park in restricted zones during home visits, with costs borne by employing healthcare providers rather than staff or local authority. Delivery plan with costings and eligibility criteria required within six months.

motions.motion_title: Withdraw single-unitary bid; back North + South Worcestershire authorities
motions.motion_text_summary: Withdraw the single-unitary bid for the whole of Worcestershire and instead back North and South Worcestershire authorities, citing the Shape Worcestershire survey showing public preference for two unitaries. Defeated by the Reform-led administration.

motions.motion_title: Affirm scientific consensus on man-made climate change
motions.motion_text_summary: The council agrees with the scientific consensus that man-made climate change exists, supported by evidence of rising global temperatures and extreme weather events. The climate-affirmation motion PASSED against the Reform minority, same pattern as Warwickshire's reaffirmation.

motions.motion_title: No Free Lunch: discontinue Full Council buffet lunches
motions.vote_result: Result not located in available coverage
motions.motion_text_summary: Discontinue the practice of providing a buffet lunch at Full Council meetings as a symbolic council-tax-payer-first cost-saving measure.

motions.motion_title: Oppose any future expansion of Leicester City boundaries (LGR context)
motions.motion_text_summary: Oppose any future expansion of Leicester City Council boundaries as part of LGR. All Reform members voted AGAINST. Carried 23-22 with one Labour abstention (Cllr Jewel Miah).

motions.motion_title: Redirect £2m net zero funding to flood defences
motions.motion_text_summary: Reallocate £2m previously earmarked for net zero / decarbonisation work to flood prevention infrastructure. Reform branded the previous allocation 'Net Stupid Zero money'. Green Cllr Naomi Bottomley criticised the false-binary framing.

motions.motion_title: Restrict flags flown on council buildings to Union Jack, St George's Cross + council flags
motions.motion_text_summary: Approve new corporate flag protocol restricting council buildings to the Union Jack, St George's Cross and council flags (limited national-flag-of-visiting-head-of-state exceptions). Voting bloc: 1 Conservative and 1 Independent voted with Reform; 1 Reform councillor voted against. 26-against bloc was the Labour / Conservative / Green / Lib Dem opposition. RCN and Unite condemned the policy as anti-LGBT.

motions.motion_title: Express solidarity with Jewish communities + stand against all hate crime
motions.motion_text_summary: Reaffirm commitment to standing firm against all hate crime including antisemitism (citing CST data) and raise awareness to support the safety of Jewish residents. Withdrawn at Full Council after ex-Reform Cllr Robert Bloom resigned 26 Aug 2025 over alleged use of racial slurs against a neighbour, political optics had soured. Lesson in motion discipline failing when group internal-conduct is concurrent.

motions.meeting_type: Cabinet (NOT Full Council motion, subsequently call-in defeated)
motions.motion_title: Drop 2030 / 2045 net zero targets and refocus sustainability strategy
motions.vote_result: Cabinet approved; call-in defeated 5-4 at Place & Resources Overview & Scrutiny (19 Aug 2025)
motions.motion_text_summary: Cabinet resolution to no longer retain net zero in own operations by 2030 and across residents/businesses by 2045. Sustainability strategy revised to replace 'climate impact' references with 'environmental impact'. Decision called in by Lib Dem Cllr Rosie Humphreys; scrutiny panel voted 5-4 in favour of upholding the Cabinet decision (5 Reform against the call-in). First Reform unitary to drop a 2030 target. Process route Cabinet not Full Council motion.

motions.meeting_type: Democracy & Standards Committee, to be referred to Full Council
motions.motion_title: Constitutional amendment creating fixed 'Priority Administration Business' item at start of every Full Council meeting
motions.vote_result: Referred to Full Council for approval
motions.motion_text_summary: Amend the constitution to create a fixed agenda item at the outset of every Full Council meeting where the administration can table a motion up to 7 days before the meeting (e.g. to debate national-importance items at local level). Pushes public participation and opposition business back. Opposition: 'showboating', 'reducing opportunities for scrutiny'.

motions.motion_title: Replace four scrutiny boards with a single Overview & Scrutiny Committee
motions.motion_text_summary: Reform proposal carried at the 20 May 2026 annual meeting to scrap three of the council's four scrutiny committees, leaving a single Overview & Scrutiny Committee. Opposition spoke against but were out-voted.

motions.motion_title: Rescind the Climate Emergency and Biodiversity Emergency Declarations
motions.motion_text_summary: Rescind the 2019 Climate Emergency and 2021 Biodiversity Emergency declarations and redirect resources to practical interventions via a future Cabinet report.
motions.outcome_note: Passed 17 Jun 2026: council "undeclared" both the 2019 climate and 2021 biodiversity declarations. No division numbers in press; moderngov minutes not yet published (checked 6 Jul 2026).

motions.motion_title: School Uniform Support Scheme
motions.motion_text_summary: Opposition motion responding to the new Reform administration's withdrawal of the universal school uniform support scheme; asks Cabinet to review the decision and justify the claimed £1.3m saving.
motions.outcome_note: Defeated 17 Jun 2026; Reform (58/63) voted against reinstating the universal voucher scheme; targeted ~£700k scheme stands.

motions.motion_title: Repeal of the Climate Emergency Declaration
motions.motion_text_summary: Rescind the Climate Emergency declaration; officers to identify all strategies, targets and budgets dependent on it; future environmental activity judged on affordability and statutory duty. 16 Reform signatories.
motions.outcome_note: Passed 48-15 on 24 Jun 2026; replaced with a "balanced framework" test (VfM, statutory duty, deliverability, resident impact, local environmental benefit).

motions.motion_title: Non-continuation of City of Sanctuary accreditation + Stronger Communities Strategy
motions.motion_text_summary: Confirm the council will not progress City of Sanctuary (asylum/refugee-welcome) accreditation; officers to develop a locally-owned 'Stronger Communities Strategy'.
motions.outcome_note: Debated 24 Jun 2026 but NO published minutes or accessible press report confirms the vote (checked 6 Jul 2026). Do not record as passed until CMIS minutes publish. Passage likely given Reform 58/75.

motions.motion_title: Review of Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO)
motions.motion_text_summary: Cabinet to commission an evidence-based review of HMOs (scale, condition, neighbourhood impact) and report on additional/selective licensing or enforcement under the Housing Act 2004.
motions.outcome_note: Agreed 24 Jun 2026; council admitted in debate it holds no full HMO list. No division numbers.

motions.motion_title: Fairer parking on Wearside
motions.motion_text_summary: Opposition motion to reintroduce 'Free After 3pm' city-centre parking, guarantee cash/contactless options, and end free parking for councillors at St Mary's Car Park.
motions.outcome_note: Passed as amended by Reform 24 Jun 2026: investigate restoring free-after-3pm city centre parking.

motions.motion_title: Rescind the 2019 Climate Emergency declaration / scrap Net Zero Newcastle 2030
motions.motion_text_summary: Reform administration to bring a motion cancelling the 2019 climate emergency and ending Net Zero Newcastle 2030; council says it has identified >£2m of savings (incl. £2.19m by buying non-electric refuse lorries).
motions.outcome_note: On the published 8 Jul 2026 Full Council agenda (item 10). Net Zero Newcastle 2030 already scrapped by executive action 26 May 2026; the 2019 declaration itself awaits this vote.

motions.motion_title: Leather Museum relocation - cost transparency
motions.mover: Cllr Elaine Williams (Leader) + Cllr Nicky Barker (Deputy)
motions.motion_text_summary: Reform-moved motion requiring full disclosure within 21 days of all costs of the previous administration's Leather Museum relocation (feasibility, legal, storage), publication of the lease/licence signed 5 May 2026 (two days before the election), and the cost of reversing the decision.
motions.outcome_note: Resolved 22 Jun 2026 via a Conservative amendment carrying the same disclosure resolution (relocation costs, 5 May 2026 lease/licence terms, £47,550 feasibility study, reversal costs) with 21-day deadlines softened to "without further delay".

motions.motion_title: Reconsider relocation of Walsall Leather Museum
motions.mover: Cllr A. Nawaz + Cllr K. Hussain
motions.vote_result: Passed (all except the 7 Conservative members present)
motions.motion_text_summary: Opposition motion calling on the Reform Cabinet to reconsider the Leather Museum relocation and commission an officer report including the full cost of not proceeding.
motions.outcome_note: Resolved 22 Jun 2026 (official decision note item 9): Cabinet to reconsider the relocation with a full officer report incl. costs of not proceeding.

motions.motion_title: Streetly Cemetery grave memorials and edgings policy review
motions.motion_text_summary: Opposition motion urging the Reform Cabinet to review and amend policy to allow memorials and edgings on graves at Streetly Cemetery.
motions.outcome_note: Approved 22 Jun 2026 (item 11): Cabinet to urgently review the draft memorials policy and consider allowing memorials/edgings at Streetly and all borough cemeteries.

motions.motion_title: Support for translation services
motions.motion_text_summary: Green motion asking the council to state it values its ~£283k translation service, rebutting Reform leaflet claims it was for people who 'refuse to integrate'. Reform voted against; fell 38-30.

motions.motion_title: Ipswich Northern Bypass / Route Protection
motions.motion_text_summary: Labour motion to reaffirm support for the Ipswich Northern Bypass and submit a business case by Sept 2026; a Reform amendment replaced the specifics with a general 'consider all options' review. Amended motion passed.

motions.motion_title: Rescind climate emergency declaration and net zero targets
motions.motion_text_summary: Reform Leader confirmed Suffolk is 'looking to undeclare' its climate emergency and remove net-zero targets, expected to be formally reversed at the 16 July Full Council. Not yet tabled/voted.
motions.outcome_note: Meeting confirmed for 16 Jul 2026 (Endeavour House, 2pm); agenda publishes ~5 days ahead so the motion is not yet on a published agenda (checked 6 Jul 2026).

motions.motion_title: Educational attainment among disadvantaged pupils (Education Summit + Poverty Commission)
motions.motion_text_summary: Notes disadvantaged-pupil attainment below national average; calls for a Lancashire Education Summit and a Poverty Commission. A Reform friendly amendment (Cllr Joel Tetlow) streamlining to an officer-led summit was carried; substantive motion carried as amended.

motions.motion_title: Permanent national ban on fracking
motions.motion_text_summary: Motion to ask Government to replace the shale-gas moratorium with a permanent national ban. A Tetlow/Pickup (Reform) amendment was carried on a recorded vote and became the substantive motion, which then carried.

motions.motion_title: Review of non-statutory Net Zero commitments and cessation of voluntary carbon reporting
motions.motion_text_summary: Reform motion: Cabinet to review all non-statutory net-zero decisions, ensure net-zero does not override value-for-money in procurement, cease voluntary carbon reporting except where legally required, and review the Pension Fund's ESG/net-zero targets against fiduciary duty. Lib Dem amendment lost; substantive motion carried.

motions.motion_title: Reformed Inclusion & Fairness Policy (replacing the EDI approach)
motions.motion_text_summary: Reform motion requiring a 'Reformed Inclusion & Fairness Policy and Delivery Plan' to Cabinet within 12 weeks, reframing EDI around structural reform, unbiased recruitment and measurable goals, 'prioritising practical improvements over symbolic gestures'. Carried.

motions.motion_title: Support for Northern Powerhouse Rail
motions.motion_text_summary: Opposition motion condemning the pledge to scrap Northern Powerhouse Rail and seeking funding for the Poulton-Fleetwood and Colne-Skipton links. On a recorded vote the substantive (amended) motion was lost.

motions.motion_title: Objection to Morgan & Morecambe Offshore Windfarm onshore cable route through Fylde
motions.motion_text_summary: Reform motion instructing the Chief Executive to write to the Energy Secretary objecting to the onshore cabling route through Fylde (disruption to residents, tourism, farmland) and demanding alternatives. Carried.

motions.motion_title: Civic Pride and playing the National Anthem at the start of Full Council
motions.motion_text_summary: Reform motion to play the National Anthem at the start of each Full Council and ask Cabinet to consider a Civic Pride Action Plan (incl. an annual Pride of Lancashire Awards). Opposition amendment lost; substantive motion carried on a recorded vote.

motions.motion_title: Defend local democracy / oppose cancellation of local elections
motions.motion_text_summary: Reform motion: write to the Secretary of State seeking assurance local elections will not be cancelled and requesting repeal of s.87 Local Government Act 2000 (power to cancel elections without a Commons vote). Carried on a recorded vote.

motions.motion_title: Tourist Travel in Kent (Motion for Time Limited Debate)
motions.motion_text_summary: Calls on the Cabinet Member for Highways to publish a plan to mitigate summer Entry/Exit System and Operation Brock traffic, and on Government to fund offline queuing at Sevington.

motions.motion_title: Protecting our Farmers (Motion for Time Limited Debate)
motions.motion_text_summary: Eight-point motion to prioritise Kent food in public procurement, support countryside pursuits, a Deer Management Plan, agricultural apprenticeships and rooftop-not-farmland solar. A Reform amendment recognising existing Executive work was agreed; amended motion approved.

motions.motion_title: Water Resilience (Motion for Time Limited Debate)
motions.motion_text_summary: Asks the Executive to press Southern Water for quarterly CSO spill reporting, ring-fencing of regulator fines and citizen-science bathing-water testing. Deferred on the Chairman's determination.
motions.outcome_note: Not debated at the 21 May 2026 AGM; the Chairman deferred the MTLD to the 16 Jul 2026 County Council meeting.

motions.motion_title: Review of Council Procedure Rules / Question Time
motions.motion_text_summary: States the Procedure Rules stifle scrutiny of the directly-elected Labour Mayor and Cabinet; asks the Monitoring Officer to review the rules and report to the Elections & Democratic Structures Committee. Carried 38-0-2 (Labour backed it).

motions.motion_title: Rescind the Doncaster Sheffield Airport reopening borrowing decision (£57m / £193m)
motions.vote_result: Passed as amended (loan reaffirmed with conditions)
motions.motion_text_summary: Reform's original motion sought to rescind the £57m/£193m airport borrowing. An amendment (Cllr Jason Charity) replaced rescission with safeguards (unredacted lease, S151 assurance, exit strategy); amendment and substantive motion carried 45-6-1. Net effect: the loan was reaffirmed with conditions, reported as a Reform U-turn.

motions.motion_title: Corporate Parenting in decision-making
motions.motion_text_summary: Resolves that reports include a section assessing impact on Children in Our Care and Care Leavers. Seconded by a Reform councillor. Tabled at the 22 May Annual Council; outcome not yet on the public record.
motions.outcome_note: Carried unamended on a show of hands with cross-party support at the 22 May 2026 AGM; verified from the official webcast (minutes publish with the 18 Sep 2026 agenda).

motions.motion_title: Reinstatement of the Peaks and Dales railway line (Matlock-Buxton)
motions.motion_text_summary: Council supports reinstating the Matlock-Buxton line and asks Cabinet to support the scheme and advocate within EMCCA and nationally. Reported passed.

motions.motion_title: Keep the Peak District National Park Free to Access
motions.mover: Cllr Alex Dale (Leader of the Opposition)
motions.motion_text_summary: Conservative motion (Park's 75th anniversary) that it remain free to access in perpetuity, challenging Reform Leader Alan Graves's reported '£1 entry' remark. A Reform amendment on Park funding was added; both amendment and amended motion carried.

motions.motion_title: Condemnation of racism + power for Group Leaders to remove members proven racist
motions.motion_text_summary: Conservative motion (prompted by conduct cases against Reform members) to condemn racism and let Group Leaders remove any member proven to have behaved in a racist manner. Reform refused to support it, calling it 'undemocratic'; defeated.

motions.motion_title: Protecting Local Highways from the Impact of National Housing Targets
motions.motion_text_summary: Conservative motion to write to Government for fairer developer S106/S278 contribution rules and to review five years of agreements. Tabled at the 14 May Full Council/AGM.
motions.outcome_note: Robertson amendment (softened "demanding" to "requesting"; reframed around the Infrastructure Levy, LURA 2023; added CIL review) accepted by mover Clarke and carried on a show of hands. Confirmed in draft minutes attached to the 9 Jul 2026 agenda.

motions.motion_title: Support for families with the cost of school uniform and equipment
motions.motion_text_summary: Opposition motion criticising the Reform administration's retained but minimal school clothing assistance (total budget ~£1,000 p.a.) as 'not fit for purpose'; calls for Select Committee scrutiny.
motions.outcome_note: Wright amendment (deleted "far too low and not fit for purpose"; welcomed the Sep 2026 branded-uniform legislation) accepted by mover Carr and carried on a show of hands. Confirmed in draft minutes.

motions.motion_title: Council 'will not be bound by the 2019 and 2025 declarations of Climate Emergencies' (Council Plan amendment)
motions.motion_text_summary: An amendment to the new 'Recalibrating Warwickshire' Council Plan (not a standalone notice of motion) stating the council will not be bound by the 2019/2025 climate emergency declarations; supported by the ruling Reform group. Council Plan with the amendment passed 31-24.

motions.motion_title: Preserve the Council's climate emergency / net zero commitments (Council Plan amendment)
motions.motion_text_summary: A Green amendment to the Council Plan adoption (not a standalone NoM) to retain the climate/net-zero focus. Three Conservatives backed it with the Lib Dems but it was defeated by the rest of the Conservatives and Reform.

motions.motion_title: Protecting the Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression (Notice of Motion 1)
motions.motion_text_summary: Notice of motion at the Council AGM, withdrawn by signatories before debate. NOTE: this was the meeting at which Reform LOST control of Worcestershire.

motions.motion_title: Motion of no confidence in the Leader of the Council (Notice of Motion 2)
motions.motion_text_summary: No-confidence motion in Reform Leader Cllr Jo Monk; withdrawn after Monk resigned as Leader that morning. A cross-party alliance then elected Green Cllr Matt Jenkins as Leader, ending Reform control of Worcestershire.

motions.motion_title: Councillor behaviour (LGA 'Debate Not Hate') (Notice of Motion 3)
motions.motion_text_summary: Cross-party motion backing the LGA 'Debate Not Hate' campaign, condemning abuse of councillors. Broad support in debate; recorded outcome not in available minutes.

motions.motion_title: Northern Ireland Troubles (Legacy and Reconciliation) Act / Operation Banner veterans
motions.motion_text_summary: Reform motion to write to the NI Secretary urging statutory safeguards for Operation Banner veterans and a non-adversarial legacy process, and to reaffirm the Armed Forces Covenant. Adopted.

motions.motion_title: Church Lane Bus Route (Whitwick)
motions.motion_text_summary: Reform motion requesting an officer report to the Highways/Transport scrutiny committee within six months on Arriva Service 12 along Church Lane, Whitwick (safety, punctuality, usage). Adopted.

motions.motion_title: Save Our Borough (opposition to forced Local Government Reorganisation)
motions.motion_text_summary: Notes the 11,000-signature petition against forced LGR submitted to the Secretary of State and opposes merging Newcastle-under-Lyme with Stoke-on-Trent in a North Staffordshire authority. Resolves to reaffirm opposition to LGR, keep the Borough standalone, call on the incoming Prime Minister and Secretary of State to scrap forced Staffordshire mergers, and asks the Leader and Chief Executive to seek a meeting.

motions.motion_title: Protection of Council-Owned Green Spaces (Fields in Trust)
motions.motion_text_summary: Endorses the previous administration's programme protecting up to 88 council-owned green spaces via Fields in Trust Deeds of Dedication and Local Plan protections, warning the new Leader's Local Plan position (Cabinet 23 Jun 2026) and potential LGR put these at risk; requires progress reports to Cabinet and Scrutiny and asks the Leader to urge Staffordshire CC to protect College Fields (Madeley) and Hoon Avenue playing fields.

motions.motion_title: Withdrawal from Local Government Association membership
motions.motion_text_summary: Single-sentence Reform motion: withdraw Newcastle-under-Lyme Borough Council from Local Government Association membership with immediate effect. No supporting rationale in the motion text.

motions.motion_title: Prioritising Frontline Policing and Value for Money (PCC's £2m private security marshal scheme)
motions.vote_result: Amended and passed (Reform amendment by Cllr Kevin Crook)
motions.motion_text_summary: Original Conservative motion opposed the PCC's proposed 18-month £2m private security marshal scheme, wanting the money reallocated to frontline police and PCSOs. Reform amendment (Crook/Hamilton-Gray) replaced outright opposition with support for the Police and Crime Panel's scrutiny request plus a Chief Executive letter demanding transparent, evidence-based decision-making before committing the Crime Prevention Fund reserve; the amended version carried.

motions.motion_title: Community Impact of Asylum Accommodation
motions.motion_text_summary: Notes resident concerns about concentrations of HMOs and asylum-dispersal accommodation (pressures on services, parking, waste, amenity, cohesion). Resolves to write to the Home Secretary seeking transparency and advance notification of placements, seek Home Office information on HMO use under government contracts, and commission a scrutiny report on impacts on County Council services. Carried overwhelmingly with cross-party support.

motions.motion_title: Maintaining Professional Standards, Workforce Sustainability and Fair Employment Practices in Leicestershire's Specialist SEND Services
motions.motion_text_summary: Notes concerns about proposed changes to staffing structures and role requirements in specialist SEND services, warning poorly managed restructuring harms morale, retention and continuity. Requests a report to Children and Families Overview and Scrutiny covering the future model of early-years SEND advisory support, professional qualifications, staff/union engagement and employment-law compliance.

motions.motion_title: Bus Services in Wigston (Arriva service changes)
motions.motion_text_summary: Criticises Arriva's Wigston service changes (47/48/49 replaced by a more complex network) for poor consultation, longer two-bus journeys and cutting estates off from GPs, the LRI and the station. With council's consent an altered motion carried: continue engaging Arriva to review the changes and work via the Enhanced Bus Partnership on community engagement ahead of future changes (dropping the Traffic Commissioner demand).

motions.motion_title: Review of Concessionary Bus Pass Travel Restrictions
motions.motion_text_summary: Conservative opposition motion asking the East Midlands CCA and Mayor Claire Ward (Lab) to identify funding to remove the 9:30am weekday restriction on concessionary bus passes and introduce free all-day travel for pass holders; movers argue the restriction blocks early medical appointments, work and volunteering.

motions.motion_title: Suspend all Work on Local Government Reorganisation
motions.motion_text_summary: Argues the Government moved the LGR goalposts by cutting the optimal unitary population threshold from 500,000 to 350,000 without consultation and opposes the forced merger of Broxtowe, Gedling and Rushcliffe with Nottingham City; if passed the council writes to MHCLG requesting the LGR project be halted pending a needs-based assessment. Conservative group has signalled support. Context: the Reform administration recently cut motion debate time from 60 to 45 minutes.

motions.motion_title: Pavement parking: preparing for prohibition and civil enforcement powers (English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026)
motions.vote_result: Pending (meeting postponed for heat; reconvenes 13 Jul 2026)
motions.motion_text_summary: Welcomes the Act enabling local transport authorities to prohibit pavement parking; requests a Cabinet Member report on preparing for the powers (enforcement options, hotspot mapping, village exceptions), preparatory officer work now, and a Leader letter pressing the Transport Secretary for a commencement timetable.

motions.motion_title: Strategic review of the council's VCFSE strategy
motions.vote_result: Pending (meeting postponed for heat; reconvenes 13 Jul 2026)
motions.motion_text_summary: Notes the VCFSE sector leverages £3.74 external for every £1 WNC invests; asks Cabinet for a joint strategic review covering incubator grants, external-funding help, multi-year funding timetables, co-production, and a possible social value and localism premium, concluding in time for the 2027-28 budget.

motions.motion_title: Disability inclusion: re-establish the Disabled People's Forum + directorate disability champions
motions.vote_result: Pending (meeting postponed for heat; reconvenes 13 Jul 2026)
motions.motion_text_summary: Cites Scope's 2025 Disability Price Tag (£1,095/month) and the 28.6% disability employment gap; resolves to re-establish the Disabled People's Forum (dormant since Oct 2023), create disability champions across directorates on the social model, revisit the EDI policy and update the Annual Equalities Report.

motions.motion_title: Opposing loss of local democratic oversight in Government planning reforms (national scheme of delegation)
motions.vote_result: Pending (meeting postponed for heat; reconvenes 13 Jul 2026)
motions.motion_text_summary: Moved by the Reform Leader of the Council against the national scheme of delegation (Planning and Infrastructure Act 2025) shifting planning decisions from councillors to officers: WNC 'will not accept councillors being reduced to bystanders'; officers to maximise member involvement within the law; report on powers lost; public guidance note; letter to Ministers demanding restoration of meaningful member involvement.

motions.motion_title: Opposition Priority Business: business rates reform and high street support
motions.vote_result: Pending (meeting postponed for heat; reconvenes 13 Jul 2026)
motions.motion_text_summary: Responds to the Apr 2026 business rates reform/revaluation: confirmation of the pubs/live-music 15% relief, scrutiny report on Supporting Small Business Relief, s47 Local Discounts policy report, High Street Business Support Programme scoping, CIL prioritisation of town centres, High Street Rental Auctions update, and a Leader letter to the Chancellor pressing permanent RHL reductions.

motions.motion_title: Fly the Ukraine flag on Ukraine Independence Day (exception to Reform flag policy)
motions.vote_result: Pending (meeting postponed for heat; provisionally 16 Jul 2026)
motions.motion_text_summary: Requests an exception to the Reform administration's flag policy so the Ukrainian flag flies from Council buildings on 24 Aug 2026 (Ukraine Independence Day), a direct challenge to the flag policy from the Conservative benches.

motions.motion_title: High Street Revival: use Community Right to Buy and High Street Rental Auction powers
motions.vote_result: Pending (meeting postponed for heat; provisionally 16 Jul 2026)
motions.motion_text_summary: Says 16 months on, the Reform administration has yet to use its early-recipient Community Right to Buy and High Street Rental Auction powers on long-term empty shops in Wellingborough, Rushden, Kettering, Corby and market towns; resolves a High Street Revival Policy, a Renewal Taskforce and a public register of long-term empty commercial property.

motions.motion_title: Independent highways expert engagement for the Local Plan and Local Transport Plan

motions.motion_text_summary: Urges engagement of independent highways experts to quantify development impacts on highways and rights of way in the new Local Plan and Local Transport Plan, with transparent cross-boundary engagement with neighbouring authorities.

lancashire_cc.amendment_rule: Only one amendment per motion; must be submitted in writing immediately following the mover's speech.
lancashire_cc.content_restrictions: Motions cannot rescind resolutions from the previous 12 months, seek to act beyond Council powers, or include defamatory or unlawful content (Standing Order 34).

kent_cc.source: Kent CC Constitution (last amended 6 May 2025), detail not located in available open-web sources; would require direct PDF retrieval.
kent_cc.note: Kent has 81 councillors. The Lord's Prayer and Illegal Migration Emergency motions were processed through the standard notice-of-motion route, so the constitutional plumbing is workable. Detail to be captured by the constitutions research running separately.

durham.note: Durham is a single unitary covering the County Durham area. Reform passed the Climate Emergency rescission as a stand-alone Full Council motion, so the notice-of-motion route is open to majority groups. Procedural-rule detail not located.

doncaster.note: Mayor-council model. Full Council motions cannot bind the directly-elected mayor's executive functions, see Mayor Jones' refusal to enact the flag policy. Procedural-rule detail not located.

derbyshire_cc.note: The 25 March 2025 allowances motion was tabled by the Leader and carried; demonstrates that the administration-led notice-of-motion route is the standard play. Procedural-rule detail not located.

lincolnshire_cc.note: The 3 March 2026 Green Masterplan adoption ran via Executive followed by Full Council ratification rather than the notice-of-motion route. Procedural-rule detail not located.

staffordshire_cc.note: The 9 October 2025 climate rescission was a standard notice-of-motion at Full Council by Cabinet Member Mynors. So the route is open. Procedural-rule detail not located.

nottinghamshire_cc.note: No Full Council climate-rescission motion has been tabled despite the cabinet member's public stance. The administrative caution is documented, see LSE Grantham Institute brief. Procedural-rule detail not located.

warwickshire_cc.note: Reform governs as minority. The 22 July 2025 climate-reaffirmation motion was tabled by the Green group, with a Conservative friendly amendment, the opposition route is fully available. Procedural-rule detail not located.

worcestershire_cc.note: Reform runs as minority. The 11 September 2025 meeting saw 4 notices of motion (1 service-quality / 1 LGR / 1 climate / 1 buffet). The opposition Lib Dem group ran 3 of the 4. So opposition groups have at least 3 motion slots per meeting, more permissive than LCC's 2.

leicestershire_cc.note: Minutes show standard mover/seconder/amendment flow. Detail not located.

north_northamptonshire.note: Standard Full Council notice-of-motion route used for the flags policy. Procedural-rule detail not located.

west_northamptonshire.note: Reform administration is REWRITING the constitution (13 Nov 2025 Democracy & Standards proposals) to insert a fixed 'Priority Administration Business' agenda slot at the top of every Full Council meeting. Pending approval. This is the only council in the cohort actively re-engineering its standing orders to elevate administration business above opposition motions.

key_findings: CLIMATE EMERGENCY RESCISSION is the single most replicated Reform play: tabled and passed at Kent (50-21-3, 19 Sep 2025), Durham (62-14-17, 16 Jul 2025) and Staffordshire (9 Oct 2025). Lincolnshire dropped its 2050 carbon-neutral target without rescinding (no declaration existed). West Northants dropped 2030/2045 targets at Cabinet. Leicestershire redirected £2m at Cabinet. Nottinghamshire administration position only. Lancashire and Derbyshire have NOT done it at Full Council level. Warwickshire (32-22) and Worcestershire (28-20) tabled REAFFIRMATION motions and beat Reform, both councils where Reform is in minority.

FLAGS / UNION-FLAG-ONLY POLICY is the second-most replicated play, passed at Lancashire (17 Jul 2025), Doncaster (10 Jul 2025, 32-14-6), North Northamptonshire (Jul 2025, 40-26-1), Kent (Cabinet, May 2025), Durham (Cabinet, May 2025), West Northants (similar policy in place), Nottinghamshire (£75K capital allocation Oct 2025). At Doncaster the Labour mayor refused to enact; at all county councils the cabinet implemented. Lancashire has done a Full Council motion AND a Cabinet review.

MOTION DRAFTING LESSON, amendment-friendly motions pass with more legitimacy. LCC's Reform Free Speech motion (Cllr Evans) ACCEPTED an Independent (Cllr Ali) amendment adding 'without inciting hatred and division / Nolan Principles compliance' and consequently passed clean. LCC's Reform Flags motion REJECTED the scrutiny-committee amendment and passed on Reform votes alone. The 'accepted amendment' version reads as cross-party in the press; the rejected-amendment version reads as partisan ramming. Worth scripting amendment-tolerance into standing motion templates.

CULTURALLY-CHARGED MOTIONS that DEFEATED or were WITHDRAWN: NNC Jewish-solidarity motion (Sep 2025) WITHDRAWN after concurrent Reform councillor racism scandal, procedurally avoidable if internal-conduct is managed. Kent VAWG-centred motion (Jul 2025) DEFEATED by Reform majority, a free-rebuttal opportunity to opposition ('Reform voted against VAWG action'). Kent Illegal Migration Emergency (Mar 2026) DEFEATED on the facts; the supporting 5-page report contained terror-cell language that did not survive scrutiny. LESSON: declarative 'emergency' motions need fact-checked supporting reports OR they invite the rebuttal that landed the motion in the bin.

FISCAL POLITICAL-CLASS-CUTS PLAYS, Derbyshire's Mar 2025 allowance freeze passed clean (good Reform play) but the BOLT-ON cut of the opposition leader's SRA produced the 'gutter politics' rebuttal. CLEAN allowance freezes are politically free; PARTISAN cuts of opposition-leader allowances are paying-political-rent. Future cohort should split these into two separate motions and only pass the clean one.

STRUCTURAL EXPLOITATION OF STANDING ORDERS, West Northants is alone in the cohort actively rewriting its constitution to elevate administration motions ABOVE opposition motions and public participation (Nov 2025 Democracy & Standards). This is a tactical play, mid-term, worth observing for replication implications.

THE NOC / MINORITY-COUNCIL TRAP, Warwickshire, Worcestershire, Leicestershire, North Northants (sometimes), West Northants. In these councils, the Reform group does NOT have an outright majority and has either lost (Warwickshire climate, Worcestershire climate, Leicestershire LGR) or had to choose Cabinet routes (West Northants net zero) over Full Council motions. Implication: do not recommend whip-dependent motions in NOC councils until coalition arithmetic is checked.

MAYOR-COUNCIL TRAP, Doncaster's Reform majority passes motions but Mayor Jones (Labour) refuses to enact. Same shape would apply at any directly-elected-mayor council in the new 14. Motions in these councils are press-pressure only.

NOT YET DONE BY ANY COUNCIL IN COHORT: (a) Pension fund / LGPS ESG mandate review (LCC has LCPF exposure but no motion tabled). (b) Forensic supplier-audit motion / Companies House cross-reference of donor-supplier networks. (c) Foreign-trip register / publish-all-overseas-travel motion. (d) Consultancy-spend register (publish every consultancy >£25K). (e) Outside-bodies appointment review (compulsory-resignation-from-conflicts). (f) Mass-deportation-of-failed-asylum motion (Kent failed on facts; lesson is to keep narrower). (g) Public-sector-equality-duty review motion (the legal Achilles heel of all DEI plays). All of these are white-space for the 15 new Reform councils.

VOTE-COUNT DATA QUALITY, of the 36 motions catalogued, only 11 have a precise vote count in available sources. Local press tends to skip exact counts. The shepwayvox / Blog Preston / LGC corpus are best sources; council democracy portals would supply the rest but most don't index per-vote data outside the minute PDFs. Reform's HQ should make recording exact vote counts a discipline expectation, the press uses them, opposition uses them, and they harden the narrative.
